content5.ptxt: The engine control computer uses the lock-up control solenoids (SL and DSU) to perform lock-up control according to driving conditions.

atten4.ptxt: The solenoid (DSU) controls the lock-up clutch pressure according to the input torque.

content5.ptxt: During torque converter lock-up control (ON/OFF), the engine control computer compares the turbine speed (NT) and engine speed (NE) to detect mechanical failure of the lock-up control solenoids (SL and DSU).
If DTCs for other lock-up control solenoid (SL and DSU) circuits are output at the same time, it is necessary to troubleshoot the DTCs other than P0741/64 and P2757/64 first.

item.ptxt: Be sure to perform this after inspecting and adjusting the engine.
Perform the test at normal operating CVT fluid temperature (50 to 100°C).
Perform the test with no electrical load, the A/C OFF and the brake OFF.
Lock-up control is not performed when the CVT fluid temperature is 40°C or less and the vehicle speed is 60km/h or less, or when the CVT fluid temperature is 5°C or less.
Lock-up control is not performed when the engine coolant temperature is 30°C or less.
The lock-up OFF vehicle speed varies according to the ON/OFF status of the electrical load, A/C and brake.

item.ptxt: Initializing the learned values clears both the G sensor 0 point learning and CVT hydraulic pressure learning values, so when replacing the parts in the table below, be sure to perform both G sensor 0 point learning and CVT hydraulic pressure learning after performing AT/CVT learned value initialization.
Continuously Variable Transaxle Assembly
Engine Control Computer
Oil Pressure Sensor
Yaw Rate Sensor
After performing AT/CVT learned value initialization, be sure to perform G sensor 0-point learning first, and then CVT hydraulic pressure learning.
Be sure to place the vehicle on a level surface and perform 0 point learning.
Do not subject the vehicle to vibration while 0 point learning is in progress.
